q-82702.name: Question 1
q-82702.problem:
$$
{P}_{B\to C}=[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 1 \\ 1 & 0 & 1 \\ -3 & 1 & 3\end{aligned}]
$$

 

The change-of-coordinates matrix from the basis $B=\{{b}_{1},{b}_{2},{b}_{3}\}$ to the basis $C=\{{c}_{1},{c}_{2},{c}_{3}\}$ is given above. Find $[x]_{C}$ given that $x=3{b}_{1}+{b}_{2}+5{b}_{3}.$
q-82702.worked_solution:
First, notice that since $x=3{b}_{1}+{b}_{2}+5{b}_{3},$ we have

$$
[x]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 1 \\ 5\end{aligned}].
$$

 

Given the coordinates of $x$ relative to $B$ and the change-of-coordinates matrix from $B$ to $C,$ we find the coordinates of $x$ relative to $C$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}[\,x\,]_{C} & ={P}_{B\to C}[\,x\,]_{B} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 1 \\ 1 & 0 & 1 \\ -3 & 1 & 3\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}3 \\ 1 \\ 5\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}9 \\ 8 \\ 7\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

q-113539.problem:
The change-of-coordinates matrix from the basis $B$ to the basis $C$ and the coordinates of the vector $x$ relative to the basis $B$ are given below. What is $[x]_{C}?$ 

$$
{P}_{B\to C}=[\begin{aligned}-2 & 2 \\ -3 & 1\end{aligned}],\,[x]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 5\end{aligned}]
$$
q-113539.worked_solution:
Given the coordinates of $x$ relative to $B$ and the change-of-coordinates matrix from $B$ to $C,$ we find the coordinates of $x$ relative to $C$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}[\,x\,]_{C} & ={P}_{B\to C}[\,x\,]_{B} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-2 & 2 \\ -3 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}2 \\ 5\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}6 \\ -1\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

The change-of-coordinates matrix from the basis $B$ to the basis $C$ and the coordinates of the vector $x$ relative to the basis $B$ are given below. What is $[x]_{C}?$ 

$$
{P}_{B\to C}=[\begin{aligned}-2 & -2 \\ -1 & 3\end{aligned}],\,[x]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}5 \\ -4\end{aligned}]
$$
q-82498.worked_solution:
Given the coordinates of $x$ relative to $B$ and the change-of-coordinates matrix from $B$ to $C,$ we find the coordinates of $x$ relative to $C$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}[\,x\,]_{C} & ={P}_{B\to C}[\,x\,]_{B} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-2 & -2 \\ -1 & 3\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}5 \\ -4\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ -17\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

The change-of-coordinates matrix from the basis $B=\{{b}_{1},{b}_{2},{b}_{3}\}$ to the basis $C=\{{c}_{1},{c}_{2},{c}_{3}\}$ is given above. Find $[x]_{C}$ given that $x=4{b}_{2}-2{b}_{1}-3{b}_{3}.$

First, notice that since $x=4{b}_{2}-2{b}_{1}-3{b}_{3},$ we have

$$
[x]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 4 \\ -3\end{aligned}].

$$
\begin{aligned}[\,x\,]_{C} & ={P}_{B\to C}[\,x\,]_{B} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2 & 0 & 1 \\ 3 & -2 & 0 \\ 1 & 1 & 3\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 4 \\ -3\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-7 \\ -14 \\ -7\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

q-36484.name: Question 5
q-36484.problem:
The change-of-coordinates matrix from the basis $B$ to the basis $C$ and the coordinates of the vector $x$ relative to the basis $B$ are given below. What is $[x]_{C}?$ 

$$
{P}_{B\to C}=[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 \\ -4 & 3\end{aligned}],\,[x]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 4\end{aligned}]
$$
q-36484.worked_solution:
Given the coordinates of $x$ relative to $B$ and the change-of-coordinates matrix from $B$ to $C,$ we find the coordinates of $x$ relative to $C$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}[\,x\,]_{C} & ={P}_{B\to C}[\,x\,]_{B} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 \\ -4 & 3\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}2 \\ 4\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-6 \\ 4\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

q-82601.name: Question 6
q-82601.problem:
The change-of-coordinates matrix from $B$ to $C$ and the coordinates of the vector $x$ relative to the basis $C$ are given below. What is $[x]_{B}?$ 

$$
{P}_{B\to C}=[\begin{aligned}3 & 2 \\ 4 & 3\end{aligned}],\,[x]_{C}=[\begin{aligned}7 \\ 6\end{aligned}]
$$
q-82601.worked_solution:
We will use the change-of-coordinates formula in the form

$$
[\,x\,]_{B}={P}_{C\to B}[\,x\,]_{C}.
$$

First, we need to find the change-of-coordinates matrix ${P}_{C\to B}$ from $C$ to $B.$ To do that, we compute the inverse of ${P}_{B\to C}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{P}_{C\to B} & ={P}_{B\to C}^{-1} \\  & ={[\begin{aligned}3 & 2 \\ 4 & 3\end{aligned}]}^{-1} \\  & =\frac{1}{3\cdot 3-4\cdot 2}[\begin{aligned}3 & -2 \\ -4 & 3\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}3 & -2 \\ -4 & 3\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we compute $[\,x\,]_{B}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}[\,x\,]_{B} & ={P}_{C\to B}[\,x\,]_{C} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}3 & -2 \\ -4 & 3\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}7 \\ 6\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}9 \\ -10\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

q-82706.name: Question 7
q-82706.problem:
The change-of-coordinates matrix from $B$ to $C$ and the coordinates of the vector $x$ relative to the basis $C$ are given below. What is $[x]_{B}?$ 

$$
{P}_{B\to C}=[\begin{aligned}7 & 4 \\ 12 & 7\end{aligned}],\,[x]_{C}=[\begin{aligned}4 \\ 5\end{aligned}]
$$
q-82706.worked_solution:
We will use the change-of-coordinates formula in the form

$$
[\,x\,]_{B}={P}_{C\to B}[\,x\,]_{C}.
$$

First, we need to find the change-of-coordinates matrix ${P}_{C\to B}$ from $C$ to $B.$ To do that, we compute the inverse of ${P}_{B\to C}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{P}_{C\to B} & ={P}_{B\to C}^{-1} \\  & ={[\begin{aligned}7 & 4 \\ 12 & 7\end{aligned}]}^{-1} \\  & =\frac{1}{7\cdot 7-12\cdot 4}[\begin{aligned}7 & -4 \\ -12 & 7\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}7 & -4 \\ -12 & 7\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we compute $[\,x\,]_{B}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}[\,x\,]_{B} & ={P}_{C\to B}[\,x\,]_{C} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}7 & -4 \\ -12 & 7\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}4 \\ 5\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}8 \\ -13\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

q-37154.name: Question 8
q-37154.problem:
The change-of-coordinates matrix from $B=\{{b}_{1},{b}_{2}\}$ to $C=\{{c}_{1},{c}_{2}\}$ is given below. Find $[x]_{B}$ given that $x=-3{c}_{1}-2{c}_{2}.$

$$
{P}_{B\to C}=[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 \\ -2 & -4\end{aligned}]
$$
q-37154.worked_solution:
We will use the change-of-coordinates formula in the form

$$
[\,x\,]_{B}={P}_{C\to B}[\,x\,]_{C}.
$$

First, we need to find the change-of-coordinates matrix ${P}_{C\to B}$ from $C$ to $B.$ To do that, we compute the inverse of ${P}_{B\to C}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{P}_{C\to B} & ={P}_{B\to C}^{-1} \\  & ={[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 \\ -2 & -4\end{aligned}]}^{-1} \\  & =\frac{1}{1\cdot (-4)-(-2)\cdot 3}[\begin{aligned}-4 & -3 \\ 2 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-2 & -\frac{3}{2} \\ 1 & \frac{1}{2}\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Notice that since $x=-3{c}_{1}-2{c}_{2},$ we obtain 

$$
[x]_{C}=[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ -2\end{aligned}].
$$

 

Now, we compute $[\,x\,]_{B}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}[\,x\,]_{B} & ={P}_{C\to B}[\,x\,]_{C} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-2 & -\frac{3}{2} \\ 1 & \frac{1}{2}\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}-3 \\ -2\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}9 \\ -4\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

[x]B=PC→B[x]C.

q-82707.name: Question 9
q-82707.problem:
The change-of-coordinates matrix from $B=\{{b}_{1},{b}_{2}\}$ to $C=\{{c}_{1},{c}_{2}\}$ is given below. Find $[x]_{B}$ given that $x=5{c}_{1}-{c}_{2}.$

$$
{P}_{B\to C}=[\begin{aligned}5 & 10 \\ 2 & 5\end{aligned}]
$$
q-82707.worked_solution:
We will use the change-of-coordinates formula in the form

$$
[\,x\,]_{B}={P}_{C\to B}[\,x\,]_{C}.
$$

First, we need to find the change-of-coordinates matrix ${P}_{C\to B}$ from $C$ to $B.$ To do that, we compute the inverse of ${P}_{B\to C}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{P}_{C\to B} & ={P}_{B\to C}^{-1} \\  & ={[\begin{aligned}5 & 10 \\ 2 & 5\end{aligned}]}^{-1} \\  & =\frac{1}{5\cdot 5-2\cdot 10}[\begin{aligned}5 & -10 \\ -2 & 5\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 \\ -\frac{2}{5} & 1\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Notice that since $x=5{c}_{1}-{c}_{2},$ we obtain

$$
[x]_{C}=[\begin{aligned}5 \\ -1\end{aligned}].
$$

Now, we compute $[\,x\,]_{B}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}[\,x\,]_{B} & ={P}_{C\to B}[\,x\,]_{C} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 \\ -\frac{2}{5} & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}5 \\ -1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}7 \\ -3\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

$$

$$
[\,x\,]_{B}={P}_{C\to B}[\,x\,]_{C}.
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}{P}_{C\to B} & ={P}_{B\to C}^{-1} \\  & ={[\begin{aligned}3 & -4 \\ -5 & 6\end{aligned}]}^{-1} \\  & =\frac{1}{3\cdot 6-(-4)\cdot (-5)}[\begin{aligned}6 & 4 \\ 5 & 3\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-3 & -2 \\ -\frac{5}{2} & -\frac{3}{2}\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

$$
[x]_{C}=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -2\end{aligned}].

q-113599.problem:
$$
B=\{[\begin{aligned}4 \\ 3\end{aligned}],[\begin{aligned}6 \\ 5\end{aligned}]\},\,[x]_{S}=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 0\end{aligned}]
$$

The basis $B$ of ${R}^{2}$ and the coordinates of the vector $x$ relative to the standard basis $S$ are given above. Find $[x]_{B}.$
q-113599.worked_solution:
We will use the change-of-coordinates formula in the form

$$
[\,x\,]_{B}={P}_{S\to B}[\,x\,]_{S}.
$$

First, recall that the change-of-coordinates matrix from $B$ to $S$ is the matrix whose columns are the vectors of $B$ relative to the standard basis $S.$ As a result, we have

$$
{P}_{B\to S}=[\begin{aligned}4 & 6 \\ 3 & 5\end{aligned}].
$$

Now, we need to find the change-of-coordinates matrix ${P}_{S\to B}$ from $S$ to $B.$ To do that, we compute the inverse of ${P}_{B\to S}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{P}_{S\to B} & ={P}_{B\to S}^{-1} \\  & ={[\begin{aligned}4 & 6 \\ 3 & 5\end{aligned}]}^{-1} \\  & =\frac{1}{4\cdot 5-6\cdot 3}[\begin{aligned}5 & -6 \\ -3 & 4\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{5}{2} & -3 \\ -\frac{3}{2} & 2\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we compute $[\,x\,]_{B}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}[\,x\,]_{B} & ={P}_{S\to B}[\,x\,]_{S} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{5}{2} & -3 \\ -\frac{3}{2} & 2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}2 \\ 0\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}5 \\ -3\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

$$
B=\{[\begin{aligned}5 \\ 3\end{aligned}],[\begin{aligned}6 \\ 4\end{aligned}]\},\,[x]_{S}=[\begin{aligned}8 \\ 6\end{aligned}]
$$

The basis $B$ of ${R}^{2}$ and the coordinates of the vector $x$ relative to the standard basis $S$ are given above. Find $[x]_{B}.$
q-113603.worked_solution:
We will use the change-of-coordinates formula in the form

$$
[\,x\,]_{B}={P}_{S\to B}[\,x\,]_{S}.
$$

First, recall that the change-of-coordinates matrix from $B$ to $S$ is the matrix whose columns are the vectors of $B$ relative to the standard basis $S.$ As a result, we have

$$
{P}_{B\to S}=[\begin{aligned}5 & 6 \\ 3 & 4\end{aligned}].
$$

Now, we need to find the change-of-coordinates matrix ${P}_{S\to B}$ from $S$ to $B.$ To do that, we compute the inverse of ${P}_{B\to S}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{P}_{S\to B} & ={P}_{B\to S}^{-1} \\  & ={[\begin{aligned}5 & 6 \\ 3 & 4\end{aligned}]}^{-1} \\  & =\frac{1}{5\cdot 4-6\cdot 3}[\begin{aligned}4 & -6 \\ -3 & 5\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2 & -3 \\ -\frac{3}{2} & \frac{5}{2}\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we compute $[\,x\,]_{B}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}[\,x\,]_{B} & ={P}_{S\to B}[\,x\,]_{S} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2 & -3 \\ -\frac{3}{2} & \frac{5}{2}\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}8 \\ 6\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 3\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

$$

The bases $B$ and $C$ of ${R}^{2}$ and the coordinates of the vector $x$ relative to the basis $C$ are given above. Find $[x]_{B}.$
q-82618.worked_solution:
Let's denote the vectors of $B$ and $C$ as $\{{b}_{1},{b}_{2}\}$ and $\{{c}_{1},{c}_{2}\}$, respectively.

The change-of-coordinates matrix from $C$ to $B$ is a matrix whose columns are the vectors of $C$ relative to the basis $B.$

Hence, we need to find the coordinates of ${c}_{1}$ and ${c}_{2}$ relative to the basis $B.$ We can do this simultaneously by considering the matrix

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}| & | & | & | \\ {b}_{1} & {b}_{2} & {c}_{1} & {c}_{2} \\ | & | & | & |\end{aligned}].
$$

Now, we simply reduce the left-hand side to reduced row-echelon form using Gaussian elimination:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 & 3 & -2 \\ 3 & 10 & 4 & 3\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+(-3){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 & 3 & -2 \\ 0 & 1 & -5 & 9\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :={R}_{1}+(-3){R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 18 & -29 \\ 0 & 1 & -5 & 9\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the change-of-coordinates matrix ${P}_{C\to B}$ is

$$
{P}_{C\to B}=[\begin{aligned}18 & -29 \\ -5 & 9\end{aligned}].
$$

Finally, we compute $[\,x\,]_{B}:$

$$

B={[12],[37]},C={[12],[20]},[x]C=[3−1]

The bases B and C of R2 and the coordinates of the vector x relative to the basis C are given above. Find [x]B.

a
[10]

[126]
c
[15−4]

[14−8]

[−114]

EXPLANATION

Let's denote the vectors of B and C as {b1,b2} and {c1,c2}, respectively.

The change-of-coordinates matrix from C to B is a matrix whose columns are the vectors of C relative to the basis B.

Hence, we need to find the coordinates of c1 and c2 relative to the basis B. We can do this simultaneously by considering the matrix M=[||||b1b2c1c2||||].

Now, we simply reduce the left-hand side to reduced row-echelon form using Gaussian elimination:

M=[13122720]R2:=R2+(−2)R1∼[1312010−4]R1:=R1+(−3)R2∼[10114010−4]

Therefore, the change-of-coordinates matrix PC→B is

PC→B=[1140−4].

Finally, we compute [x]B:

[x]B=PC→B[x]C=[1140−4][3−1]=[−114]
